extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and engineers building PRMs, dataset creators for LLM reasoning and formal-verification pipelines
extracted.subtask_description: Creating step-level labeled training data for Process Reward Models (PRMs) by converting LLM-generated formal reasoning traces into binary correct/incorrect labels using formal verification tools, and using those labels to fine-tune PRMs and evaluate them with Best-of-K and step-level metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step-level binary labels (correct/incorrect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign step-level error labels [ys1, ys2, ..., ysk] ∈ {0,1}^k which indicate whether each individual reasoning step is correct (1) or incorrect (0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper uses binary labels as the supervision signal for PRM training; labels are balanced in FOVER-40K (50% correct / 50% incorrect). Training uses cross-entropy on these labels and PRMs output the token “correct” or “incorrect” per step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use formal verification tools for accurate label annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use automated formal verification tools (e.g., Z3 for first-order/SMT, Isabelle/HOL for theorem proving) to assign step-level error labels automatically instead of human annotation or Monte Carlo roll-outs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FormalVerification(p, [s1...sk]) outputs ysi = 1 if step si is correct, 0 otherwise. Example: unsatisfiable combination of premises ∧ ¬hypothesis implies entailment confirmed by SAT/SMT solver. Emphasized benefits: accurate annotation, no human annotation, fewer LLM calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generate formal solutions in formats compatible with verification tools
rubrics_metrics.description: LLM-generated solutions must follow a syntax and format that can be parsed/checked by the chosen formal verification tool (Isabelle or Z3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use few-shot demonstrations to guide format; generate multiple solutions until one has valid format; filter out invalid formats (e.g., illegal symbols) before verification. The pipeline includes format verification and conversion steps; invalid-format proofs are discarded or corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step-level formal verification (independent per-step checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify correctness of individual reasoning steps independently by checking that each step logically follows from the provided context and preceding (assumed-correct) results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For logic tasks, check satisfiability of premises ∧ preceding results ∧ ¬(step conclusion). For theorem-proving with Isabelle, insert 'sorry' in all but the step under test to type-check the step syntactically and semantically, running Isabelle once per step to determine correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle format parsing with isolated syntactic checking (Isabelle 'sorry' strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Isabelle's 'sorry' placeholder to allow syntactic/step parsing when full proof is incomplete, enabling per-step checking even if other steps are invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert 'sorry' in all steps except the one being verified so Isabelle can type-check and parse that step. Also use the 'sorry' trick to filter syntactically invalid outputs during format verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filter and discard invalid-format proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect and remove proofs that cannot be parsed by the verification tool (e.g., illegal symbols or invalid syntax), rather than attempting to label them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format verification returns errors (e.g., Inner syntax error). The pipeline discards or retries generation until a syntactically valid proof is obtained; invalid-format items are not given labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine step-independent verification with solution-level checks for assumption-related errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that step-independent verification may miss errors that depend on incorrect assumptions or discharged assumptions; therefore, combine with solution-level verification to identify final-step errors related to assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example limitation: proofs that use an undischarged assumption may pass step-independent checks but fail solution-level verification. The suggested remedy is to combine both verification modes to catch such mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced labels in training data
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct training datasets with balanced proportions of 'correct' and 'incorrect' step labels (FOVER-40K has 50% error rate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During training set construction and fine-tuning, use mechanisms like mask_history: True in LLaMA-Factory to use only the last step if needed and ensure label balance for stable PRM training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training objective and output convention for PRMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine-tune LLM-based PRMs on the step-level binary classification task with cross-entropy loss; PRMs are implemented as models that output per-step probabilities for the token 'correct'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loss L = sum_i (ysi log rsi + (1-ysi) log(1-rsi)). Implementation detail: fine-tune in text-generation mode to output 'correct'/'incorrect'; extract logits for those tokens and apply softmax to get step-level score rsi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input / postprocessing format for PRM inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide each step as a conversation-style input where the expected output is a single token 'correct' or 'incorrect'; during inference extract logits immediately preceding the dummy labels and compute probability for 'correct'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This format allows extracting per-step logits in causal LLMs. For other PRMs with different token conventions (e.g., '+'/'-'), substitute tokens accordingly. Use softmax over the two target tokens for scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best-of-K selection protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Best-of-K to evaluate PRMs by generating K candidate solutions per problem and using the PRM to score each solution; the solution score is the minimum per-step score across all steps, and the highest-scoring solution is selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard in PRM evaluation: generate K=7 solutions with few-shot prompts and temperature 0.5; for each candidate compute per-step 'correct' probability and choose candidate with maximum min-step probability. Evaluate selected solution accuracy on downstream benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best-of-K evaluation settings & sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting Best-of-K results, generate K=7 step-by-step solutions with few-shot demonstrations and temperature 0.5; evaluate on 250 randomly sampled examples per dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prior work (Cobbe et al., 2021; Li et al., 2023) for consistency. Use dataset-specific prompt engineering (line breaks between steps, few-shot examples per task).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step-level verification evaluation metric (AUROC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure PRM performance on step-level binary classification (error detection) using AUROC on datasets with human-annotated step labels (e.g., ProcessBench).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ProcessBench includes labels only for the earliest error in each trace; use steps up to the first error for evaluation. Report AUROC per benchmark and averaged metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best-of-K performance metric (accuracy) on reasoning benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Report Best-of-K selection accuracy (e.g., percentage of problems where the selected candidate is correct) on reasoning benchmarks such as GSM8K, MATH, AQuA-RAT, AIME, FOLIO, LogicNLI, ANLI, HANS, MMLU, BBH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report per-benchmark and average Best-of-K accuracy, and compare to baseline PRMs and prior PRMs. Use consistent example sampling and prompt settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether improvements over baselines are statistically significant using paired bootstrap tests, reporting significance at p < 0.05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper marks statistically significant improvements with an asterisk (p < 0.05, paired bootstrap). Use paired bootstrap to compare Best-of-K or AUROC improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficiency criterion: minimize number of LLM calls per solution for labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer data-creation methods that require fewer LLM calls per step/solution (FOVER requires 1 LLM call per solution + verification, whereas Monte Carlo roll-outs require multiple continuations e.g., 8 × #steps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 4 contrasts methods: MC roll-outs (Math-Shepherd) require multiple LLM calls per step, leading to high compute; FOVER needs a single LLM generation per solution and uses automated verification, reducing computational cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on stronger LLMs for annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer annotation pipelines that do not require using stronger models as judges to produce labels (i.e., do not distill stronger-LM judgments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FOVER's verification-based labels do not require stronger LLMs; alternatives that use stronger LLM annotators risk merely distilling other models rather than producing independently verified labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: No human annotation preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to construct PRM training data without human annotation to reduce cost and inter-annotator disagreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human annotation is costly and suffers from low inter-annotator agreement (e.g., discarding 30% of annotated solutions in prior work). FOVER seeks to eliminate human labels by using formal verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label accuracy as a desideratum
rubrics_metrics.description: Training data labels should be accurate (reflecting true step correctness) to produce effective PRMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal verification provides accurate deterministic judgments (unsatisfiable/satisfiable checks, proof validity). The paper emphasizes accuracy of formally-verified labels relative to noisy Monte Carlo labels or heuristic perturbations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset selection criteria (diversity, simplicity, generalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select source problems for formal-data construction based on diversity of reasoning forms, syntactic simplicity for verification, and expected generalization to informal tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FOVER selects FLDx2 for formal logic due to diversity and GSM8K-level math for simplicity and generalization considerations. When designing datasets, balance expressivity (diverse deductive rules) and tractability for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training regime and hyperparameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine-tune all model parameters (no parameter-efficient adapters used), use AdamW optimizer, linear warmup/decay, epoch and batch settings as chosen by validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors used 1 epoch, batch size 32, learning rate selection based on validation Best-of-K across candidate LR values (1e-6 to 1e-5). While implementation details, these choices are prescribed as the training setup for PRMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation on unseen tasks to measure cross-task generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate PRMs on tasks substantially different from training tasks (e.g., NLI, BBH, MMLU-Pro-NoMath) to measure cross-task generalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FOVER-PRMs are validated on unseen tasks and compared against baseline PRMs and existing PRMs to show formal-to-informal transfer and cross-task generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to backbone model strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that PRMs trained on FOVER data constructed from weaker models still improve or are comparable when used with stronger backbone LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper evaluates Qwen 3 4B (stronger model) fine-tuned on FOVER-40K generated by weaker models and reports improved or comparable Best-of-K performance across benchmarks, indicating robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-efficiency desideratum
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for datasets where relatively small subsets already give competitive performance (e.g., 10K instances comparable to 40K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ablation shows PRMs trained on 10K instances of FOVER-40K already achieve performance comparable to full dataset, suggesting data-efficient label construction via formal verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational resource and verification throughput considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Design verification pipelines to be CPU-parallelizable and fast: Z3 verifies formal-logic datasets quickly; Isabelle verification per step should be performant when parallelized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported runtimes: Z3 verifies all datasets in less than 10 minutes (single process); Isabelle verifies each step ≈3 seconds, with annotation using 40 parallel Isabelle processes on multi-core CPUs. Use parallel CPU runs for scalability.
